events.title: Grounded spec built
events.reasoning: The product clearly supports creating multi‑stage sourcing events (RFP/RFQ/auction), inviting vendors, placing bids, and awarding contracts, as confirmed by both catalog.json and prd‑procol‑sourcing.md. It also includes team‑based user management, matching the PRD’s requirements. However, the PRD specifies that the phone field must accept any 10‑digit number, while the backend only checks length, not that the characters are digits—creating a concrete spec‑vs‑product gap. This discrepancy is a high‑priority test case because it could let invalid phone numbers pass validation.

deltas.prdSays: Accept any 10-digit number; reject malformed input politely (PRD §4.3, §5).
deltas.productDoes: The API checks phone LENGTH (rejects 9 or 11 digits) but NOT that characters are digits — it accepts a 10-char value containing letters. The frontend enforces digits-only, so the API is more lenient than the UI.

cases.scenario: Simultaneous surrogate bid submissions on the same event
cases.preconditions: Buyer has created event EV567 with an open bid window; no existing bids for vendor V001; two client sessions are ready to send requests at the same time.
steps: 1. In session A, send POST /api/events/EV567/bids with payload {vendor_id:"V001", price:5000, comment:"Surrogate bid"}.
2. In session B, concurrently send the identical POST request.
4. Query the database for bids linked to event EV567 and vendor V001.
5. Verify that only one bid record exists.
cases.testData: Positive: bid payload {vendor_id:"V001", price:5000, comment:"Surrogate bid"}.
cases.expectedResult: One request succeeds with 201 Created; the other receives 409 Conflict with message "Duplicate surrogate bid for vendor V001". Database contains exactly one bid row for vendor V001 on event EV567; the failed transaction is rolled back with no partial data. Concurrency control (optimistic lock or unique constraint) functions correctly.
